#### Import packages

Import the different libraries we will need.

```{r, message=FALSE}
library("tidyverse")
library("curl")
```

#### Load data

Import the data from Kaggle ("https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/piotrgrabo/breastcancerproteomes?select=77_cancer_proteomes_CPTAC_itraq.csv")

```{r}
# Create data folders
dir.create("../data/_raw", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Download data
curl_download(
  url = "https://www.kaggle.com/api/v1/datasets/download/piotrgrabo/breastcancerproteomes",
  destfile = "../data/_raw/breastcancerproteomes.zip",
  mode = "wb"
)

# Unzip
unzip("../data/_raw/breastcancerproteomes.zip",
      exdir = "../data/_raw")

# Remove ZIP archive
invisible(file.remove("../data/_raw/breastcancerproteomes.zip"))
```

```{r, warning=FALSE}
# Load datasets into environment
file_names <- c(
  "77_cancer_proteomes_CPTAC_itraq.csv",
  "clinical_data_breast_cancer.csv",
  "PAM50_proteins.csv"
)

proteomes <- read_csv(str_c("../data/_raw/", file_names[1]), show_col_types = FALSE)
clinical  <- read_csv(str_c("../data/_raw/", file_names[2]), show_col_types = FALSE)
pam50     <- read_csv(str_c("../data/_raw/", file_names[3]), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

### Duplicate samples

For three of the patients, duplicate samples were collected. First we check the correlation between duplicate samples to be sure that duplicates from the same patient are consistent.

```{r}
# set up variables
sample_cols  <- str_subset(names(proteomes), "TCGA")
patients     <- str_split_i(sample_cols, "[_.]", 1)
dup_patients <- unique(patients[duplicated(patients)])

# compute correlation matrices for duplicate samples
dup_cor_matrices <- map(dup_patients, function(p) {
  proteomes |>
    select(all_of(sample_cols[patients == p])) |>
    cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs") |>
    round(3)
}) |>
  set_names(dup_patients)

dup_cor_matrices
```

#### Mean duplicate protein expression levels

Seeing as the three duplicate measurements correlate well, we merge the duplicates so that each patient has only one measurement. Consequently, patients having more than one sample will have a single value per protein (the average of their replicates).

```{r}
proteomes_dupmean <- proteomes |>
  # 1. long format only protein expression cols
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(RefSeq_accession_number, gene_symbol, gene_name),
               names_to = "sample",
               values_to = "log2_ratio") |>
  
  # 2. patient ID: tumors get TCGA-AO-A12D format, controls keep their own name
  mutate(patient_id = if_else(str_detect(sample, "TCGA"),
                              str_c("TCGA-", str_split_i(sample, "[_.]", 1)),
                              sample)) |>
  
  # 3. mean per protein and patient (only the replicates actually change)
  group_by(RefSeq_accession_number, patient_id) |>
  summarise(log2_ratio = mean(log2_ratio, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  
  # 4. turn NaN's into true NA's
  mutate(log2_ratio = if_else(is.nan(log2_ratio), NA_real_, log2_ratio)) |>
  
  # 5. back to wide format
  pivot_wider(names_from = patient_id,
              values_from = log2_ratio)
```

### Renaming columns of the PAM50 file before merging

The columns in the PAM50 dataset have a slightly different naming convention:

```{r}
head(pam50)
```

In order to filter the proteomic dataset down to only the PAM50 gene reference list, we rename RefSeqProteinID to RefSeq_accession_number in the PAM50 table to get a common column name.

```{r}
pam50 <- pam50 |> 
  rename(RefSeq_accession_number = RefSeqProteinID)
```

### Merge data

#### Proteomes for only PAM50 genes

The PAM50 dataset contains genes, whose mRNA expression signatures can be used to classify breast cancer into 5 different subtypes. To compare classification by mRNA expression vs protein expression for these genes, we merge these two datasets, keeping only the expression profiles of PAM50 proteins for our study.

```{r}
# left joins to only keep the 100 reference genes for breast cancer
proteomes_pam50_joined <-  inner_join(pam50, 
                                      proteomes_dupmean, 
                                      by ="RefSeq_accession_number")

head(proteomes_pam50_joined)
```

#### Entire proteomes dataset merged with the clinical dataset

In order to utilise the clinical data for each patient, such as the RNA PAM50 classification of breast cancer subtypes, in our analysis, we join the proteomic data to the clinical dataset. As the clinical data has patient IDs in a column, we transpose the proteomic data:

```{r}
proteomes_dupmean_transposed <- proteomes_dupmean |> 
  # keep only accession numbers and expression level cols
  select(RefSeq_accession_number, 
         ends_with("CPTAC") | starts_with("TCGA")) |>
  
  # get one row pr. protein x patient
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -RefSeq_accession_number, 
    names_to = "patient_id",
    values_to = "log2_ratio") |> 
  
  # get one row pr. patient, one col pr. protein
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = RefSeq_accession_number,
    values_from = log2_ratio
  )
```

We can now join by the common column 'patient_id', called 'Complete TCGA ID' in the clinical dataset:

```{r}
final_dataset_all_genes <- left_join(
  proteomes_dupmean_transposed, 
  clinical, 
  by = c("patient_id" = "Complete TCGA ID")
)

head(final_dataset_all_genes)
```

#### PAM50 filtered proteomes merged with clinical data

```{r}
proteomes_pam50_transposed <- proteomes_pam50_joined |> 
  # keep only accession numbers and expression level cols
  select(RefSeq_accession_number, 
         ends_with("CPTAC") | starts_with("TCGA")) |> 
  
  # get one row pr. protein x patient
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -RefSeq_accession_number, 
    names_to = "patient_id",
    values_to = "log2_ratio"
  ) |> 
  
  # get one row pr. patient, one col pr. protein
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = RefSeq_accession_number,
    values_from = log2_ratio
  )

head(proteomes_pam50_transposed)
```

Sanity check of columns removed from clinical + proteome join (delete?)

```{r}
setdiff(names(proteomes_pam50_joined),
        names(select(proteomes_pam50_joined,
                     RefSeq_accession_number, ends_with("CPTAC") | starts_with("TCGA"))))
```

left_join(), creating NA's in all clinical data columns for Control samples.

```{r}
final_pam50_filtered <- left_join(
  proteomes_pam50_transposed, 
  clinical, 
  by = c("patient_id" = "Complete TCGA ID")
)

head(final_pam50_filtered)
```

### Write final tibbles to tsv files in the data folder

```{r}
data_path <- "../data/"

write_tsv(x = final_pam50_filtered, 
          file = str_c(data_path, 
                       "01_dat_load_final_pam50_filtered.tsv"))

write_tsv(x = final_dataset_all_genes, 
          file = str_c(data_path, 
                       "01_dat_load_final_dataset_all_genes.tsv"))
```
